memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "After she left, she took off her veil and put on her widow's clothes again" - Gen 38:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In a single quiet verse, Tamar slips away, removes her disguise, and returns to her widow's clothes as though nothing had happened. To all outward appearances, life goes back to normal. Judah does not know who she was; Tamar's secret is hidden; the disguise is put away. But we know — and more importantly, God knows — what really took place.

This little verse is a reminder that things done in secret are still fully known to God. Disguises may fool people, and we may slip back into "normal" life as if a hidden act never occurred. But nothing is hidden from the Lord. "Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight" (Heb 4:13).

Both Judah and Tamar would soon discover that what was done quietly by the roadside could not stay hidden forever. In about three months, the truth would begin to show. Secret things have a way of coming to light, in God's time and often in unexpected ways (Luke 12:2).

This truth cuts two ways. It is a warning: we cannot truly hide our sin behind disguises and appearances, so it is far better to walk in honesty and integrity. And it is also a comfort: the wrongs done to us in secret, the injustices no one else sees, are seen by God — and He is a God of justice. Live before the God who sees all, both to keep from hidden sin and to trust Him with hidden hurts.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do you live as though God sees what others cannot?
Is there something hidden you need to bring into the light?
Can you trust God with secret wrongs done to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, nothing is hidden from Your sight. Keep me from secret sin, and help me to walk in honesty. And where I have been wronged in secret, I trust You, the God who sees, to bring justice. Amen.
